records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

affiliations: School of Medicine, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
records.abstract: Background Positive paediatric cancer treatment outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) significantly lag behind those in high-income countries. One reason for this disparity is high treatment abandonment rates in LMICs, defined as a failure to start or complete curative-intent therapy after a cancer diagnosis. We did a systematic review and meta-analysis to describe interventions aimed at reducing treatment abandonment in paediatric patients with cancer in LMICs. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we completed a comprehensive search of MEDLINE Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane on Oct 21, 2022, with an updated search on Oct 21, 2025. Studies were included if they met the following criteria: studied an intervention on treatment abandonment; included patients with cancer aged 18 years and younger; were conducted in LMICs as defined by the World Bank income classification; contained quantification of treatment abandonment by patients in a comparison and intervention group; and had a full-text article available. We restricted inclusion to English-language studies. We systematically assessed the quality of the studies and conducted a random-effects meta-analysis of risk ratios. Findings Among the 2263 articles identified across the two searches, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. affiliations: Cancer Epidemiology Research Program, Catalan Institute of Oncology, Bellvitge Biomedical Research Institute (IDIBELL), L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain; Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red de Epidemiología y Salud Pública (CIBERESP CB06/02/0073), Madrid, Spain; Programa de Doctorat en Medicina i Recerca Translacional, Universitat de Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain.
records.abstract: Background Regularly updated global estimates are needed to monitor progress in cervical cancer screening, a key pillar of WHO's strategy to eliminate cervical cancer. We aimed to update estimates of cervical cancer screening coverage in 194 WHO member states and eight associated countries and territories for 2022, including the first global assessment of human papillomavirus (HPV) test-based screening adoption and roll-out. Methods In this review and synthetic analysis, we used an established method to estimate standardised cervical cancer screening coverage in 2022. We used programme and population-based coverage data collected up to Jan 31, 2024, selecting the sources considered most representative of each country or territory's screening situation in 2022. Preliminary estimates were reviewed through a WHO country consultation (April-May, 2024; with additional responses received until July 2025). HPV testing coverage was estimated based on HPV test-based screening implementation levels, by country and year. Estimates were applied to 2022 populations and aggregated by region and country-income level. Findings Cervical cancer screening recommendations were identified in 161 (80%) of 202 countries, with 92 (57%) of 161 countries recommending HPV test-based screening. records.title: Perineal Urethrostomy After Urethral Stricture: Step-by-Step Surgical Technique.
affiliations: Serviço de Urologia, Hospital Federal da Lagoa, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brasil.
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Urethral stricture is a chronic narrowing of the urethral lumen caused by inflammation and iatrogenic interventions, including previous surgery and prostate cancer treatment (1). Treatment options include urethral dilation, internal urethrotomy, urethroplasty, and perineal urethrostomy. Perineal urethrostomy creates a permanent urethral meatus and is increasingly considered a primary treatment option for complex cases or patients with significant comorbidities (2, 3). It is associated with high patient satisfaction, preserved continence, and favorable voiding outcomes (4). This video presents a systematic, step-by-step description of the surgical technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 73-year-old man with complex, recurrent urethral stricture had undergone multiple reconstructive and endoscopic procedures before perineal urethrostomy in February 2026. His medical history was notable for Bowen's disease of the glans penis. Under spinal anesthesia, with the patient in the high lithotomy position, an inverted U-shaped perineal incision was made, and the bulbocavernosus muscle was dissected to expose the bulbar urethra. The perineal skin was sutured to the opened urethra, incorporating the urethral mucosal edge, corpus spongiosum adventitia, and skin edge. The dorsal urethral plate was left intact, preserving longitudinal blood flow within the corpus spongiosum. A Foley catheter was inserted through the proximal urethrotomy into the bladder. Methods Proteins were extracted from 16 samples collected from six different clothing items, proteolyzed with trypsin, and the resulting peptides were analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry using an Orbitrap Astral instrument. affiliations: Department of Pathology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY, USA. david.fooksman@einsteinmed.edu.
records.abstract: The bone marrow is a critical niche for multiple myeloma initiation, growth, and pathology. The biological and technical complexities of the bone marrow microenvironment make it challenging to study tumor physiology in situ. We have developed a thinned-bone surgical preparation for imaging the mouse tibial bone marrow. Using this approach, we have studied the spatial organization and temporal dynamics of myeloma cells, their interactions with the immune microenvironment, and the effects of acute drug treatments. In this chapter, we detail a protocol describing this procedure and present two use cases for intravital imaging to study dynamics tumors. In one study, we describe the use of photoactivation to capture live immune cells that are present within myeloma foci within the bone marrow for downstream analysis by flow cytometry or by other methods. In the second use case, we used imaging to capture effects of drug treatment in real-time in situ in the bone marrow to understand mechanisms of action and side effects.

affiliations: Department of Hematopathology, ACTREC, Tata Memorial Center, HBNI University, Room 18, CCE Building, ACTREC, Sector 22, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, 410210, India. docprt@gmail.com.
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) serves as a critical biomarker of prognosis, treatment efficacy, and clinical outcome. It captures the presence of residual tumor cells below the detection threshold of conventional microscopy. Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

records.title: Breast cancer screening in Europe and the role of general practitioners: A 32-country comparative survey.
records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is the commonest cancer in women, and screening can allow earlier-stage diagnosis. While there are European recommendations on the age-range and frequency of breast cancer screening, participation in these programmes varies substantially, and this could be due to differences in how they are organised and implemented. The role that primary healthcare professionals play in the process is unclear.We aimed to describe the breast cancer screening programmes in European countries and investigate how primary healthcare professionals are involved in this screening process.Methods A cross-sectional survey in 32 countries. Key informants with relevant expertise answered online questions about the characteristics of their screening programmes and general practitioners' (GPs') roles in this. Responses were refined through an iterative consensus process. Data were examined to identify patterns in GP engagement.Results We found important differences between European breast cancer screening systems. While most had population-based screening, four countries relied on opportunistic screening. In 15 countries GPs had little or no involvement in the process of breast cancer screening, and in 13 countries GPs had some involvement, including identifying eligible patients, issuing referrals, and following-up results. Screening uptake rates tended to be higher in countries with well-established population-based screening programmes which give little or no GP involvement.

affiliations: University of West Bohemia in Pilsen
records.journal: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
records.abstract: This review evaluates the application of deep learning (DL) for the predictive modeling of electronic materials in computer engineering. We analyzed peer-reviewed literature across four major databases, focusing exclusively on advanced architectures like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative models. Results indicate these models accurately predict critical properties, such as band gaps and thermal conductivity, for next-generation semiconductors, 2D materials, and memristors. These high accuracies are achieved because architectures like GNNs effectively capture complex 3D spatial interactions without requiring manual feature engineering. However, practical fabrication remains hindered by data scarcity, algorithmic opacity, and a profound "Sim-to-Real Gap". While DL accelerates predictive design, sustaining Moore's Law ultimately requires developing autonomous "Self-Driving Labs" and Large Material Models to bridge digital predictions with physical synthesis.

records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library was conducted to identify studies reporting the association between high-grade TB and survival outcomes in stage II-III CRC. A total of 43 studies involving 17,831 patients were included. Multivariable analysis confirmed the independent prognostic value of high-grade TB for all three outcomes. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms that high-grade TB is an independent prognostic factor in stage II-III CRC, consistently associated with worse DFS, OS and CSS. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. In cancer, this layer is not a passive coating. Its thickness, composition, charge, and nanoscale organization are altered by oncogenic signaling, dysregulated glycosyltransferases, protease-mediated shedding, and reciprocal interactions with stromal and immune cells. records.title: Risk Factors for Esophageal Candidiasis in Non-HIV Patients: A Systematic Review
records.abstract: Esophageal candidiasis is commonly associated with HIV infection but also occurs in patients without HIV. This systematic review aimed to summarize risk factors for esophageal candidiasis in non-HIV patients. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies evaluating risk factors in non-HIV populations or reporting non-HIV subgroups separately, and the findings were synthesized qualitatively. Four studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising retrospective case–control and prospective observational studies in endoscopy-based settings. Reported prevalence among non-HIV patients ranged from 0.34% to 8.99%, depending on the population and case ascertainment. Corticosteroid use was the most consistently reported risk factor (odds ratios 2.05 to 6.67), and one study found a higher risk with higher doses. Proton pump inhibitor use (odds ratio 1.66), broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure (4.55), diabetes mellitus (7.34), malignancy (8.05), and increasing age (1.02 per year) were also reported, but proton pump inhibitor use and diabetes mellitus were significant in one study and not in another. Dysphagia and odynophagia predicted esophageal candidiasis in one prospective study, whereas a retrospective study found no correlation between symptoms and endoscopic severity. METHODS: A retrospective clinicopathological analysis was performed on five cases of lung adenocarcinoma with uterine metastasis, supplemented by a literature review. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

records.title: Sex-Dependent Modulation of the Endocannabinoid System in Pain Processing
records.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly evaluated for its capacity to enhance expert human performance, yet the inverse paradigm, an AI agent supported by a human expert, is rarely studied.Here we investigate both directions of human-AI collaboration in brain tumour imaging assessment.Eleven board-certified radiologists assess 564 cases across ten datasets and four countries in a prospective, multi-reader randomised crossover reader study, predicting contrast enhancement from pre-contrast magnetic resonance imaging alone, with and without AI segmentation support.Accuracy and confidence, and their alignment, improve for both agents when each supports the other.AI support raises radiologist balanced accuracy from 0.698 to 0.743 and reduces reporting time from 45.6 to 30.6 seconds per case.Radiologist input raises the AI's balanced accuracy from 0.824 to 0.842 and its confidence-accuracy correlation from -0.078 to 0.272.Synergistic gains arise when human and AI support one another, underscoring the value of bidirectional augmentation over replacement.

records.title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

records.abstract: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are a transient, highly migratory embryonic stem cell population unique to vertebrates. During development, they give rise to diverse tissues, including craniofacial cartilage, peripheral neurons, glia, melanocytes, and components of the cardiac outflow tract. As NCCs migrate through complex environments, precise spatial and temporal regulation of gene expression is needed to coordinate migration and developmental fate. Defects in NCC development and migration can result in a broad class of disorders known as neurocristopathies (NCPs), including craniofacial abnormalities, Hirschsprung’s disease, and neuroblastoma. Despite the importance of NCC migration during development, many of the molecular mechanisms regulating this process are still not fully understood. One mechanism that enables spatial regulation of gene expression is RNA localization, the transport of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) to specific subcellular regions. Previous work, including studies from our lab, demonstrated that in other migratory cell types, specific mRNAs localize to cellular protrusions and contribute to efficient migration. Interestingly, in these systems, disruption of mRNA localization alone is enough to reduce migratory efficiency, suggesting that RNA localization itself plays an important role in regulating migration. records.abstract: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. The second part examined whether food-related behaviors were associated with ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy. records.title: [Advances in precision management of aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia in breast cancer].
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
records.abstract: Endocrine therapy is a core strategy throughout the management of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, substantially reducing the risks of recurrence and death. However, treatment-related adverse events, particularly aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia (AIA), have become a major barrier to treatment adherence. Current evidence suggests that AIA cannot be explained solely by estrogen deprivation. T-cell leukemia/lymphoma 1A (TCL1A) genetic variants, interleukin-17/nuclear factor-κB-related inflammatory pathways, and an imbalance between T helper 17 and regulatory T cells may jointly contribute to its development, suggesting that AIA may represent a modifiable pathological process. Accordingly, its management should shift from symptom-oriented palliation toward a precise supportive-care model integrating risk stratification, early intervention, and long-term adherence maintenance. From a translational medicine perspective, this review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenesis of AIA, intervention trials, and the latest guidelines, and proposes a three-stage AIA management framework adapted to Chinese clinical practice (baseline assessment and prevention-stratified intervention-digital closed-loop follow-up). The framework emphasizes the importance of alleviating adverse events to maintain treatment adherence and improve long-term outcomes but requires prospective clinical validation.

records.abstract: Green tea, derived from Camellia sinensis, is a widely consumed dietary source of bioactive polyphenols. Among its major catechins, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) has been studied most extensively in cancer research. This review critically synthesizes phytochemical, molecular, preclinical, epidemiological, clinical, pharmacokinetic, and safety evidence to assess the potential role of green tea catechins in cancer prevention and treatment. Preclinical studies of breast, prostate, colorectal, lung, liver, oral, and hematological cancers indicate that EGCG modulates oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, proliferation, apoptosis, cell-cycle progression, angiogenesis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, invasion, metastasis, and epigenetic regulation. Reported molecular targets include the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, MAPK, JAK–STAT, and NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as EGFR and VEGF signaling, BCL-2 family proteins, caspases, matrix metalloproteinases, and enzymes involved in DNA methylation. A systematic review and meta-analysis reported an association between green tea or EGCG exposure and lower overall cancer risk, with variation by cancer type and study design. Clinical evidence for efficacy in established malignancies remains limited, and conventional oncological treatment remains the standard of care. records.title: Association between Alcohol Screening with Brief Intervention and Colorectal Cancer Screening Among Alcohol Users in the United States: A Cross- Sectional Study from 2022 BRFSS
records.abstract: Abstract Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) is still a major public health issue on a global scale, being the second leading cause of cancer death and the third most common cancer worldwide. Alcohol screening with brief intervention (ASBI) is recommended to reduce unhealthy alcohol use; however, whether receiving advice to reduce or quit drinking through ASBI is associated with CRC screening participation among current drinkers aged 45–75 years remains unclear. This study aimed to examine whether receiving ASBI advice to reduce or quit drinking was associated with CRC screening participation and whether this association differed by alcohol consumption intensity (moderate versus excessive drinking) Methods Data were collected from 17,845 current drinkers aged 45–75 years in 11 states administering the ASBI module of the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). The outcome was CRC screening status (up-to-date vs. not). The primary exposure was receipt of advice to reduce or quit drinking. Survey-weighted logistic regression crude and adjusted models estimated the association between ASBI advice and CRC screening. Interaction, stratified, and sensitivity analyses were also conducted. Results Overall, 70.8% of 17845 participants had up-to-date CRC screening. records.title: Co-design and feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for colorectal cancer survivors: a mix-methods study
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose Colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors experience persistent challenges that negatively affect health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While mobile health (mHealth) may offer a useful approach to survivorship care, limited user involvement and scarcity of structured programs in developing countries remain barriers. This study aimed to co-design and evaluate the feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for CRC survivors following primary treatment. Methods A mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 utilized a user-centered design framework involving 12 co-designers across nine online sessions to develop and refine the FORYOU mHealth program. Phase 2 was a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 30 CRC survivors to assess feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the 12-week program, measured by HRQoL outcomes. Results In phase 1, the co-designed program indicated above-average usability (System Usability Scale ≥ 68) and adequate acceptability (E-Acceptability Scale ≥ 24). In phase 2, the adherence rate was 73.3%; participants in the intervention group completed an average of 5.4 out of 6 sessions and accessed the app 9.7 times. Although no significant between-group difference was observed in overall HRQoL, exploratory findings were mixed. The intervention favored the subscale functional well-being ( P < 0.05; g = 1.34), whereas the control group favored the secondary outcome, fatigue. records.title: Association between health-promoting behaviour patterns and nutritional risk among colorectal cancer survivors: a cross-sectional study in a primary care setting
records.abstract: Abstract Background Colorectal cancer survivors may experience persistent nutritional problems, but the association between their health-promoting behaviour patterns and nutritional risk is poorly understood. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study in a primary care setting in Shanghai, China. Latent profile analysis identified patterns of health-promoting behaviour, and logistic regression examined their associations with nutritional risk. Results Of 207 questionnaires distributed, 203 valid responses were analysed; 58.62% of participants were men and 60.1% were aged ≥ 70 years. Three profiles were identified: high-level (n = 29, 14.3%), moderate-level (n = 91, 44.8%), and low-level (n = 83, 40.9%). Nutritional risk was present in 27.09% of participants, with prevalences of 42.2%, 18.7%, and 10.3% in the low-level, moderate-level, and high-level profiles, respectively (p < 0.001). Compared with the low-level profile, the moderate-level and high-level profiles had lower adjusted odds of nutritional risk (odds ratio [OR] 0.31, 95% CI 0.14–0.67; and OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02–0.34, respectively). Participants aged ≥ 70 years had higher odds than those aged ≤ 60 years (OR 5.25, 95% CI 1.21–33.41). A longer time since diagnosis was associated with lower odds of nutritional risk. Conclusions These findings suggest that survivors with low levels of health-promoting behaviour may warrant closer nutritional assessment in primary care. records.title: Early-onset colorectal cancer in Lebanon: clinical presentation, molecular features and outcomes in a 618-patient cohort
records.abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), diagnosed before age 50, is rising in many countries, but data from the Middle East and North Africa remain scarce. We compared the clinical presentation, pathological and molecular characteristics, and outcomes of EOCRC and later-onset colorectal cancer (LOCRC) in a Lebanese cohort. Methods This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive patients with colorectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed at a tertiary referral center in Beirut, Lebanon, between January 2017 and July 2026. Characteristics were compared between age groups with correction for multiple testing, associations with EOCRC were explored by multivariable logistic regression, and overall survival by Kaplan–Meier and Cox models. Results Of 618 patients, 92 (14.9%) had EOCRC, 35.9% of whom were aged 45–49 years; none was detected by screening colonoscopy. Compared with LOCRC, patients with EOCRC more often had a predisposing condition (inflammatory bowel disease or hereditary syndrome: 10.2% vs 2.3%; q = 0.013), a family history of colorectal cancer (29.7% vs 12.3%; q = 0.020) and mucinous or signet-ring histology (19.2% vs 8.1%; q = 0.014). records.title: Phenome wide analysis of neurological disease associated short tandem repeats in UK Biobank
affiliations: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
records.abstract: Abstract Short tandem repeat (STR) expansions cause neurological and neuromuscular disorders, but their phenotypic spectrum in unselected carriers is incompletely characterised. We performed a phenome-wide association study of 48 STR variants at 41 neurological disease loci, genotyped with ExpansionHunter in 484,561 whole-genome sequenced UK Biobank participants. Carriers were defined by published pathogenic thresholds or, where thresholds exceeded the 150-bp read length, as the top 0.01% of repeat length. Hospital inpatient ICD-10 diagnoses were tested by Firth logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and 10 genetic principal components, requiring at least five carrier cases, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. We identified 145 associations at FDR < 0.05 across 12 loci, 85 of them novel, most at DMPK (101) and TCF4 (17). DMPK expansion carriers (n = 324) had increased odds of gynaecological cancer (odds ratio [OR] 3.03, 95% confidence interval 1.46 to 5.53; nine carrier cases), including ovarian (OR 4.67, 1.75 to 9.93) and endometrial cancer (OR 3.58, 1.34 to 7.63), and of benign colonic neoplasm (OR 4.20, 1.95 to 7.82). records.title: Divergent Mutational Landscapes and Clinical Outcomes in P53-Negative High-Grade Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Versus Cervical Cancer
affiliations: Third Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
records.abstract: Abstract Objective P53 negativity is a shared diagnostic feature of both some high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) and cervical cancer, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the distinct pathogenic mechanisms and signaling dependencies that distinguish P53-negative HGSOC from P53-negative cervical cancer. Methods Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and P53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) were performed on archival HGSOC and cervical cancer cohorts. Clinical parameters were collected for P53-negative cases, followed by comprehensive molecular profiling using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS). Differentially mutated genes were subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Results Patients with P53-negative HGSOC were significantly older (≥ 50 years: 81.25% vs. 50%, P < 0.05) and exhibited a five-fold higher mortality rate (25% vs. 5%) than the P53-negative cervical cancer cohort. Molecular profiling revealed that all 16 P53-negative HGSOC cases harbored deleterious TP53 mutations, whereas P53-negative cervical cancers showed wild-type TP53 but high mutation frequencies in PIK3CA (33.33%) and TERT (27.78%); notably, the P53-negative phenotype in cervical cancer was attributable to E6 oncoprotein-driven ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation of wild-type P53 rather than to TP53 gene inactivation. records.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng
records.abstract: Nghiên cứu nhằm đánh giá mức độ chấp nhận và tính khả thi của việc lấy mẫu xét nghiệm HPV DNA trong sàng lọc ung thư cổ tử cung từ góc nhìn cán bộ y tế (CBYT) tuyến cơ sở tại Hải Phòng năm 2023. Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang, kết hợp định lượng và định tính, với khảo sát 30 CBYT và 8 cuộc thảo luận nhóm tại các trạm y tế thuộc huyện Thủy Nguyên và Vĩnh Bảo. Kết quả cho thấy 70,0% CBYT quen thuộc hoặc rất quen thuộc với phương pháp lấy mẫu. Tỷ lệ chấp nhận triển khai tại trạm y tế và tại cộng đồng lần lượt là 100,0% và 96,7%. Có 73,3% CBYT không ghi nhận khó khăn khi lấy mẫu; 93,3% đánh giá hệ thống dễ sử dụng, 93,3% tự tin khi sử dụng, nhưng 53,3% cho biết cần hỗ trợ kỹ thuật. Thảo luận nhóm ghi nhận những trở ngại liên quan đến việc phụ nữ tự lấy mẫu và nhu cầu hỗ trợ bảo quản, vận chuyển mẫu. Kết quả cho thấy mức độ chấp nhận cao và tính khả thi bước đầu từ góc nhìn CBYT. Việc mở rộng triển khai cần tăng cường đào tạo, hỗ trợ kỹ thuật, chuẩn hóa quy trình bảo quản, vận chuyển mẫu và truyền thông nâng cao nhận thức cộng đồng.

records.abstract: Abstract Background We aimed to construct a curated whole-slide image (WSI)-report dataset for bladder cancer and establish a clinically grounded benchmark for evaluating vision–language models through an open community challenge. Methods We curated a dataset of 902 deidentified bladder cancer WSIs paired with corresponding pathology reports. Seven teams submitted distinct modeling frameworks. Performance was assessed using a clinically weighted composite metric integrating word-overlap scores (ROUGE-L, BLEU-4), keyword matching, and embedding-based semantic similarity. Expert mean opinion scores (MOS) were obtained, and the correlation between the weighted-sum score and expert-assigned MOS was analyzed. Results Two modeling strategies emerged: end-to-end generative architectures and multi-step classification-then-generation pipelines. Among individual submissions, the top-ranked multi-step pipeline achieved the highest main-diagnosis accuracy (48/50), whereas end-to-end models showed greater sensitivity to rare pathological features. The weighted-sum metric correlated strongly with MOS within each team (Spearman’s ρ, 0.65–0.91) and, on reports with clinically important misclassifications, agreed with MOS more closely than any single metric. records.abstract: Nghiên cứu nhằm mô tả chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp tại Bệnh viện Nội tiết Trung ương năm 2026. Sử dụng thiết kế mô tả cắt ngang sử dụng bộ câu hỏi EORTC QLQ-C30 và THY-34 phỏng vấn 181 người bệnh ung thư tuyến giáp đã được phẫu thuật và hiện đang khám theo dõi định kỳ tại khoa Khám bệnh, Bệnh viện Nội tiết trung ương từ 01/2026-06/2026. Đối tượng nghiên cứu chủ yếu là nữ giới (86,2%), tuổi trung bình 45,1 ± 10,9; đa số mắc ung thư tuyến giáp thể nhú giai đoạn I (97,8%). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ-C30, các lĩnh vực chức năng đạt điểm tương đối cao (75,9–85,2 điểm), điểm sức khỏe tổng quát đạt 69,1 ± 14,1; các triệu chứng nổi bật là mệt mỏi (24,3 ± 18,3), rối loạn giấc ngủ (22,7 ± 25,0) và đau (18,1 ± 16,9). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ THY-34, các lĩnh vực có điểm cao nhất là hỗ trợ xã hội (80,9 ± 23,7), tác động xã hội (56,0 ± 29,2) và triệu chứng cảm xúc (48,5 ± 22,8); các triệu chứng đặc hiệu thường gặp nhất là triệu chứng vùng cổ (26,3 ± 17,4), vấn đề về giọng nói (21,2 ± 18,6) và khó nuốt (18,3 ± 19,0). Chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp nhìn chung tương đối tốt, tuy nhiên vẫn cần quan tâm cải thiện các triệu chứng thể chất, tâm lý và xã hội.

This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. records.abstract: Childhood cancers are life-threatening diseases and are a major cause of death in children worldwide. Research shows that children with cancer are at risk for psychopathology, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety and depression. Major theories of psychopathology assign a significant role to the way people attend to and remember negative content as predictors and maintenance factors in emotional disorders. Thus, the aim of the proposed research is to delineate factors that may predict psychopathology among children with cancer. In line with central theories of emotional disorders (Mathews & MacLeod, 2005), we focus on cognitive biases involving processing threat-related information, and their relation to psychopathology. The children in the active phase of the treatment and those in remission will perform several cognitive tasks, assessing attention bias, working memory bias, and memory bias. Biases will involve stimuli related with cancer, non-cancer negative and neutral. These types of stimuli were chosen to explore whether the biases are specific to stimuli that are related to the acquired illness. Subsequently, they will be interviewed using semi-structured clinical interviews to assess the presence of emotional disorders. records.title: Molecular determinants of antibody-mediated priming to enhance detection of ctDNA
affiliations: Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research At MIT
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Liquid biopsies can enable cancer detection and monitoring yet remain limited by low amounts of ctDNA. To address this limitation, we previously introduced a monoclonal antibody (mAb) "priming agent" that transiently increased the amount of ctDNA in blood. Here, we investigated the molecular features in both the agent and the target that drive this effect. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We developed a panel of novel mAbs and other cfDNA-binding agents and characterized their interaction with cfDNA, impact on cfDNA clearance, ability to increase ctDNA recovery, and impact on cfDNA fragmentation and composition in tumor bearing mice. RESULTS: mAbs targeting either dsDNA or intact mononucleosomes increased the recovery of cfDNA and ctDNA without changing tumor fraction. mAbs with high avidity to dsDNA performed best, highlighting dsDNA as the key structural target for priming agents. One agent preserved short molecules of cfDNA associated with transcription factor binding sites and typically depleted at baseline. The Fc domain was not required for a measurable priming effect, as F(ab')2 retained priming activity. Leveraging these insights, we engineered single-chain agents using the dsDNA binding domain sso7d, expanding priming strategies beyond immunoglobulins. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the molecular features and general design principles for mAb-based priming agents to enhance recovery and detection of ctDNA.

records.title: Engineering signal transduction for closed-loop gene and cell therapies
records.abstract: Chronic diseases are still treated largely with interventions that are constitutive, intermittently administered and poorly aligned with real-time physiology. Synthetic biology is changing this paradigm by treating gene circuits as programmable genetic software that can be deployed across cellular therapeutic hardware spanning from prokaryotic to eukaryotic systems, including probiotic cells, designer cells, immune cells and stem‑cell‑derived platforms. In this framework, engineered systems can sense disease-associated signals, compute them through synthetic or repurposed transduction pathways and adjust therapeutic output to maintain physiological variables within a desired range. Closed-loop therapeutics therefore begin to merge diagnosis, treatment and prevention within the same living platform. Across metabolism, inflammation, infection, cardiovascular regulation and cancer, early mammalian systems show that endogenous sensing, intracellular computation and therapeutic actuation can be combined in clinically relevant architectures. The emerging concept of setpoint medicine captures the clinical ambition of these systems: not simply to deliver a dose, but to keep physiology within an interpretable and therapeutically desirable range. Realizing this vision will require durable and modular control circuits, hardware-aware delivery strategies, interpretable safety frameworks, controller-style performance metrics and increasingly AI-assisted design, calibration and oversight.

records.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, driven largely by tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and therapeutic resistance. Tissue biopsy, while the diagnostic gold standard, offers only a static snapshot of a constantly evolving disease, and repeated sampling is often impractical, particularly in metastatic settings. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative capable of capturing this evolving biology in real time through circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and extracellular vesicles (EVs). This review examines the biological features, analytical technologies, and clinical applications of these analytes in BC, with particular attention to two rapidly evolving areas. First, we discuss how artificial intelligence and machine learning are being applied to multi-analyte liquid biopsy data, from methylation- and fragmentomics-based classifiers for early detection to models integrating ctDNA and CTC information for resistance profiling and treatment-response prediction, while critically examining current limits in clinical validation and interpretability. records.title: Long-standing Chronic Diarrhea Associated With Intestinal Spirochetosis Incidentally Diagnosed in a Rectal Adenoma Specimen Resected by Cold Snare Polypectomy: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Endoscopy Aichi Cancer Center Hospital Aichi Japan.
records.abstract: Intestinal spirochetosis (IS) is an uncommon condition that is often asymptomatic and detected incidentally but may occasionally present with chronic diarrhea. We report a case of IS incidentally identified in the adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa of a rectal adenoma specimen resected by cold snare polypectomy. We present a case of a man in his 50s who was referred for a positive fecal occult blood test and had a history of chronic diarrhea. Colonoscopy revealed a 5-mm sessile polyp in the upper rectum, which was removed by cold snare polypectomy. Histopathological examination showed a tubular adenoma. In addition, routine hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed a characteristic false brush border on the adjacent non-neoplastic colorectal epithelium, consistent with IS. A detailed medical interview subsequently revealed chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years and prolonged close contact with a pet dog. Treatment with metronidazole (1500 mg/day for 10 days) resulted in resolution of the diarrhea. This case highlights the importance of careful histopathological examination and detailed history-taking in patients with IS.

records.title: Disparities across Colorectal Cancer Screening Modalities: Recommendations and Uptake
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States, with persistent disparities in screening rates. We examined racial and ethnic disparities in provider recommendations for CRC screening tests and screening uptake among U.S. adults eligible for screening using cross-sectional data from the 2019, 2021, and 2023 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Participants included adults aged 50-75 in 2019/2021 and 45-75 in 2023 (N=39,771). Primary outcomes were self-reported provider recommendation in the past 12 months and up-to-date status with guideline-concordant screening. In fully adjusted models accounting for socioeconomic factors and insurance, Hispanic (aOR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56-0.82), non-Hispanic Black (aOR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.67-0.98), and non-Hispanic Asian adults (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.38-0.66) were significantly less likely than non-Hispanic White adults to receive recommendations. Odds of being up to date were lower for Hispanic (aOR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.75-0.93), Asian (aOR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.51-0.68), and American Indian/Alaska Native adults (aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.55-0.96). Difference-in-differences analysis confirmed that the 2021 recommendations change increased provider recommendations by 13.4 percentage points among 45-49 year-olds. Persistent disparities in recommendation patterns highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve equity.

records.title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
records.abstract: Abstract Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

records.title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
records.abstract: Abstract Background An important application of single-cell genomics experiments is to identify genes specific to biological categories or experimental conditions. We develop ember (Entropy Metrics for Biological ExploRation), an entropy-based framework that uses Shannon’s chain rule across nested biological partitions. Four axioms characterize its Ψ score within a class of normalized entropy-decomposition scores. Results Applying ember to eight tissues from eight founder mouse strains, we find that gene specificity is often unintuitive: canonical markers can be supplanted, housekeeping genes are context-dependent, and mouse strain can drive unexpected cell type switching. Unsupervised learning on entropy metrics uncovers shared genes specialized to male gonads and kidney, as well as genes specific to non-consecutive developmental stages in the kidney. To facilitate further exploration of gene specificity in mice, we have also developed a comprehensive specificity database, along with a web interface, API and MCP server. Extending ember to a human PBMC dataset collected from 255 diverse individuals, we find that variation in PBMCs is largely localized to classical monocytes. We also find genes with unique specificity by sex, age and ancestral background. Conclusions Together, these applications establish ember as a powerful tool and provide a roadmap for elucidating the impact of human genetic variation using the murine model.

records.title: Improving surgical risk prediction through integrating automated body composition analysis: a retrospective study on colectomy surgery
records.abstract: Background: Body composition measurements may predict surgical outcomes, but current approaches are not optimized across body regions and outcome types. The added value of these measurements beyond established clinical factors remains unclear, highlighting a critical gap. Methods: This retrospective cohort study conducted across three hospitals within a tertiary health system evaluated whether computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition metrics predicted postoperative outcomes after colectomy, alone or in combination with clinical variables or the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) Surgical Risk Calculator. Of 3560 colectomy patients (2010–2023), 1621 met the inclusion criteria (a preoperative CT within 90 days with L3 visible). More than 300 features were extracted from preoperative CTs across multiple vertebral levels, including skeletal muscle area, density, fat area, and inter-tissue metrics. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality, assessed using Cox proportional hazards modeling, the concordance index (C-index), and the integrated Brier score. Secondary outcomes included complications, unplanned readmission, blood transfusion, and severe infection, and were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Brier score from logistic regression. records.title: Arctic Puffin Algorithm with local escaping operator for feature selection in high-dimensional datasets
records.abstract: Abstract Large datasets might make data mining more difficult due to their high dimensionality. To minimize the dimensionality of large datasets, feature selection is an essential step that maximizes classification accuracy by choosing the most informative features. In this study, a binary adaptation of the enhanced Arctic Puffin Optimization (EAPO) algorithm, which builds on the Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO) algorithm, is introduced within a wrapper-based framework to identify the optimal subset of features for classification tasks. To improve the search performance of APO, a local escaping operator is incorporated to effectively balance exploration and exploitation and enhance its ability to escape local optima. Furthermore, a key aspect of EAPO is the design of the transfer function, which facilitates the transformation of the continuous search space into a binary domain. To evaluate its effectiveness, three transfer functions, S-shaped, V-shaped, and U-shaped, are investigated. The proposed EAPO method is assessed on 14 benchmark datasets using the k-Nearest Neighbor classifier as the evaluation metric. To control overfitting, k-fold cross-validation employs a partitioning strategy in which the dataset is divided into k folds, and each fold is used as the test set once while the remaining folds form the training set. records.title: Lipid Metabolic Rewiring in Cancer Drug Resistance: Pathways, Networks, and Therapeutic Strategies
records.abstract: Drug resistance limits cancer therapy, and metabolic reprogramming helps tumor cells adapt to therapeutic stress. This review examines how altered lipid uptake, synthesis, storage, and oxidation support survival by changing signaling, membrane composition, energy production, redox balance, and tumor-microenvironment interactions. The SCAP/SREBP axis is a key transcriptional regulator; oncogenic and nutrient signaling (EGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, mutant p53) controls SREBP abundance and activation, and sustained SREBP activity during treatment distinguishes resistant from sensitive cells in several models, including gefitinib-resistant lung cancer and sorafenib/lenvatinib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MicroRNAs regulate these pathways post-transcriptionally, including ferroptosis-related targets (ACSL4, SLC7A11, GPX4). Inhibitors of lipogenesis, SCAP/SREBP, cholesterol metabolism, fatty-acid oxidation, lipid uptake and storage, phospholipid and sphingolipid signaling, and ferroptosis have improved drug sensitivity in preclinical models. However, many studies show only an association with resistance rather than that modulating a pathway restores sensitivity; findings vary between tumor types; and compensatory rewiring, toxicity, and limited tumor selectivity constrain single-target approaches, while miRNA-based therapeutics remain early-stage. Rational combinations guided by lipidomic and transcriptomic profiling are a priority.

records.title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer
records.abstract: Abstract Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

records.title: Intratumoral delivery of crystallized IDO1 inhibitor IDO5L does not improve tumor control in murine tumor models
records.abstract: Abstract Tryptophan (Trp) is required by both immune and tumor cells for protein synthesis and key metabolic pathways. While immune cells rely on Trp for proliferation and function, tumor cells exploit IDO1-mediated Trp degradation to evade immune surveillance. However, clinical trials have demonstrated limited efficacy of IDO1 inhibitors, likely due to insufficient tumor targeting and immune evasion strategies within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we explored a novel approach using intratumoral (IT) delivery of a crystallised IDO1 inhibitor designed for depot-based slow release. Using aggressive murine solid tumor models, we combined in vivo assessments of tumor growth with metabolic profiling to investigate treatment effects. Despite increased metabolite abundance in tumors, IT administration of the crystallised IDO1 inhibitor failed to control tumor growth compared to soluble formulations (subcutaneously or intravenously). Immune profiling confirmed that IDO1 blockade alone did not reverse immunosuppression in the TME. Interestingly, IT treatment with IDO1 inhibitor crystals significantly elevated nicotinamide riboside (NR) levels, suggesting tumor-intrinsic metabolic adaptation via the NAD⁺ salvage pathway. Similarly, local delivery of crystallised Trp did not suppress tumor progression. PASylation offers a biological alternative to the chemical PEG polymer, employing recombinant or synthetic (poly)peptides made of the small natural L-amino acids Pro, Ala and Ser which, in contrast to PEG, are biodegradable. After surgical resection of primary tumour, patients will commence RT. Patients will undergo 18 F-FMISO PET prior to RT and after two weeks of RT. Patients will be eligible for RT de-escalation (total prescribed dose 30 Gy in 15 fractions) in the absence of hypoxia on intra-treatment PET (irrespective of baseline hypoxia status). records.abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to develop and validate the C-reactive protein-albumin score (CAZ score) using a multicenter cohort, evaluating its prognostic value for cancer patients and its association with severe malnutrition and cachexia. Methods The analysis included a multicenter cohort of 6,492 cancer patients, with validation in Cohort A ( n = 4,548) and Cohort B ( n = 1,944). The CAZ score was calculated by normalizing baseline C-reactive protein and albumin levels into z-scores and combining them, then stratifying into four categories (normal, mild, moderate, severe). Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, and restricted cubic spline analysis were used to assess the CAZ score’s prognostic value for overall survival (OS). Logistic regression examined its associations with severe malnutrition and cancer cachexia, with sensitivity analysis excluding short-term mortality to test robustness. Results Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed significant stepwise differences in OS across the four CAZ score categories (71.9% vs 65.9% vs 54.9% vs 42.3%, Log-rank P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant linear dose-response relationship between the continuous CAZ score and cancer-related mortality risk ( P < 0.001). records.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
records.abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack. Combining genomic heterogeneity with baseline tumor burden (e.g., lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) or radiographic lesion dimensions), we developed a parsimonious model that predicted durable responders with high precision and specificity. Notably, the analogous population of patients treated instead with immunotherapy were not durable responders, suggesting that the selected predictors of durable responders are targeted therapy specific. records.title: Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations
records.abstract: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. records.title: Targeting oxidative phosphorylation to impair tumor-initiating properties of triple- negative breast cancer stem-like cells
records.abstract: Abstract Cancer stem-like cells (CSCs) have been implicated in tumor recurrence, therapeutic resistance, and metastatic progression, making their metabolic dependencies potential therapeutic targets. We investigated oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) as a metabolic vulnerability of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) stem-like cells and evaluated the effects of mitochondrial metabolic intervention in vitro and in vivo. Mammosphere-derived cells exhibited enhanced mitochondrial respiration. Building on our previous findings that the repurposed antimicrobials amoxicillin (AMX) and fosmidomycin sodium salt (FSS) inhibit OXPHOS, we now demonstrate that these agents also suppress mammosphere formation, reduce mitochondrial respiratory activity, and increase oxidative stress and mitophagy in CSC-like TNBC cells. In vivo, mammosphere-derived cells exhibited increased metastatic potential, as indicated by greater lymph-node enlargement and lung nodule burden, which were significantly reduced by AMX treatment. In a complementary tumor-establishment model, administration of AMX for approximately two weeks before cell implantation delayed subsequent tumor development. These findings indicate that targeting mitochondrial metabolism can impair tumor establishment and reduce metastatic-associated outcomes in a TNBC stem-like cell model. records.abstract: Rationale Glioblastoma is highly resistant to conventional therapies due to the limited penetration of chemotherapeutics across the blood-brain and blood-tumor barriers (BBB, BTB). This study investigated whether focused ultrasound (FUS)-mediated BBB/BTB disruption combined with intravenous carboplatin and stereotactic radiotherapy could improve drug delivery, tumor control, and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model. Methods F98 glioma-bearing rats were treated with a single dose of 15 Gy radiation therapy (RT), carboplatin only, carboplatin + RT, FUS + carboplatin or FUS + carboplatin + RT. Tumor progression and microenvironmental changes were monitored using multiparametric MRI (diffusion, perfusion, and vascular permeability), followed by voxel-wise clustering analysis and histopathological validation. Results The FUS + carboplatin + RT group demonstrated the strongest therapeutic benefit, compared to all other treatment groups, yielding up to a 122% increase in median survival relative to the untreated group. records.title: Interactions Between Cancer and the Nervous System: a Review of Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Cancer Neuroscience
affiliations: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review The emerging field of cancer neuroscience investigates how neural activity shapes tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. Recent research aims to define the bidirectional communication between neurons, glial cells, and tumor cells, and to clarify how neural signals influence the tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent Findings Neuronal activity promotes glioma growth via paracrine mediators such as neuroligin-3 (NLGN3), BDNF, TSP-1 and IGF-1, activating PI3K–mTOR signaling and supporting tumor proliferation. Cancer cells also exploit glutamatergic synapses, with AMPA and NMDA receptor activity driving survival and invasion, suggesting opportunities for repurposing antiseizure drugs such as perampanel. Ionic signaling through K⁺ and Ca²⁺ channels further facilitate tumor–neuron coupling. Beyond gliomas, sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs, as well as chronic stress–induced HPA axis activation, modulate angiogenesis, immune evasion, and metastasis. Summary Neural regulation of cancer encompasses neurotrophic signaling, neurotransmitter pathways, ion channel activity, and stress-mediated neuroendocrine responses, collectively shaping tumor biology and revealing novel therapeutic targets.

records.title: Identification of lead CD24 scFvs for integration into CAR T-cell therapy
records.abstract: CD24 is a heavily glycosylated surface protein reportedly expressed across a broad range of solid and hematological malignancies, making it an attractive candidate antigen for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. Using publicly available datasets, we confirmed that CD24 is broadly expressed across tumor types and, in a single CD19-negative relapse of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, remained expressed after CD19 CAR T-cell therapy. Thus, CD24 has potential both as a pan-cancer target and as a second-line or combinatorial target following antigen escape. Notably, the antigen recognition domain of the CAR, typically a single chain variable fragment (scFv) of an antibody, is a critical determinant of CAR specificity and function. We here, therefore, performed a head-to-head comparison of four CD24 second-generation 4-1BB CAR T-cells differing only in their scFv clone, specifically clones H2L3, SWA11 and GB7011–05 recognizing the protein core of CD24 and clone SN3 recognizing a CD24 glyco-epitope. The H2L3-derived CAR T-cells displayed high basal IFN-γ production whereas the SWA11-derived CAR T-cells were cytotoxic against cell lines with undetectable CD24 expression. The SN3- and GB7011–05 derived CARs were CD24-specific, and phenotypically equivalent, making them both promising candidates for further exploitation.

records.abstract: Background Tumor-associated macrophages are major contributors to the immunosuppressive microenvironment of glioblastoma (GBM), yet the upstream regulators of their pro-tumorigenic activity remain incompletely defined. Methods Bioinformatic analyses were combined with pharmacological experiments in RAW264.7 macrophages, conditioned-medium assays in GL261 cells, RNA sequencing, protein validation, and an orthotopic glioma model. Results Integrated pan-cancer analyses identified GPR84 as a prognostically adverse gene associated with an inflammatory and macrophage-enriched microenvironment in GBM. In RAW264.7 macrophages, pharmacological GPR84 activation with 6-OAU induced a mixed M2-like immunoregulatory phenotype characterized by increased STAT3 phosphorylation, CD206, TGF-β1, and extracellular IL-10 without altering total STAT3. Stattic partially attenuated STAT3 phosphorylation and CD206 induction, supporting a contributory but incomplete role for STAT3. Conditioned medium from 6-OAU-treated macrophages enhanced GL261 clonogenicity, migration, and invasion. RNA sequencing and protein validation further implicated ECM-receptor interaction and mesenchymal programming in recipient glioma cells. In an orthotopic model, implantation of GL261 cells preconditioned with medium from pharmacologically GPR84-activated macrophages resulted in increased tumor growth and shorter survival in recipient mice. records.abstract: Abstract Background The prevalence of malnutrition risk among oncology patients across a wide range of cancer types in the United States (US) has rarely been investigated. The objective of this study was to characterize malnutrition risk by demographic and cancer characteristics, and to identify potential risk factors for malnutrition risk in diverse cancer patient populations. Methods A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using Electronic Medical Record data from 2,894 adult patients living with cancer who underwent malnutrition screening at nine outpatient cancer clinics at the Huntsman Cancer Institute, with a catchment area that includes Utah, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, and Wyoming. Data were collected from January 2021 to April 2024. Malnutrition risk was evaluated using two validated malnutrition screening tools: the Malnutrition Screening Tool (MST) and NUTRISCORE. T-tests and Chi square tests of independence were used to assess differences in sociodemographic, geographic, and cancer characteristics between those with and without malnutrition risk. Logistic regression was implemented to identify potential risk factors for malnutrition risk in an outpatient cancer patient population. Results Malnutrition risk prevalence for all cancers combined was 23% according to MST and 12% according to NUTRISCORE. records.title: A universal platform for TCRα/β removal enables safer and more potent TCR therapies and autoimmune modeling
records.abstract: Adoptive T-cell therapies using tumour-specific T-cell receptors (TCRs) are limited by competition with endogenous receptors, impairing efficacy and posing risks of off-target autoreactivity. Here we present a CRISPR-based platform that selectively eliminates both endogenous TCR-α and -β chains without affecting transgenic TCRs, irrespective of codon optimization. This approach achieves >90% deletion efficiency in Jurkat and primary human T cells, enhancing expression and functional potency of transgenic receptors. Using an HLA-A*02:01-restricted DMF5 TCR, we show that dual TCR ablation boosts antigen-specific activation and cytotoxicity in vitro and enhances tumor clearance in vivo in human immune system (HIS) mice and prevents graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Targeted locus amplification showed that CRISPR-induced double-strand breaks did not alter lentiviral integration profiles, supporting genomic safety. Extending this approach to four insulin-reactive TCRs demonstrated that endogenous receptor removal increased transduction efficiency and functional activity, with one (1E6) showing selective activation and infiltration of islet grafts (SC-islets) in vivo. This study establishes a universal, safe, and scalable genome-editing platform for generating functionally precise human T cells. records.title: A map of multi-omics quantitative trait loci in a Chinese population reveals regulatory variations and disease links
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
records.abstract: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) studies have been pivotal in mapping the genetic regulation of molecular traits but have been primarily conducted in European populations, limiting insights into diverse ethnic groups. To close this knowledge gap, we conduct a large-scale multi-omics QTL analysis using blood samples from 3,102 Chinese individuals, systematically characterizing the regulatory effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation, plasma levels of 365 inflammation-related proteins, and metabolites. Our study identifies 209 protein QTLs (pQTLs) for 155 proteins and 587 metabolite QTLs (metabQTLs) for 369 metabolites. By integrating these findings with cis-methylation QTL (meQTL) from our previous work, we define the shared genetic architecture across molecular layers. Colocalization analyses reveal 3,665 pairs of shared causal variants across traits, including loci such as LHPP, with mediation evidence supporting regulatory cascades linking DNA methylation, proteins, and metabolites. To link these molecular findings to health outcomes, we perform Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, identifying 497 potential causal relationships between molecular traits and diseases, including FCRL3 for Graves’ disease and deoxycholic acid 3-glucuronide for colorectal cancer. records.title: Expanding the genetic spectrum of hereditary polyposis syndromes: a multicenter study from Argentina
affiliations: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas
records.abstract: Abstract Hereditary polyposis syndromes (HPS) predispose to colorectal cancer, yet their genetic landscape in Argentina remains underrepresented. We analyzed 177 individuals from 163 unrelated families recruited through three Argentine reference centers, including 169 index cases and eight affected relatives evaluated for segregation analyses. Genetic testing included APC and MUTYH analysis by Sanger sequencing and MLPA, complemented by multigene panels and whole-exome sequencing (WES). Variants were classified following ACMG/AMP guidelines. Germline APC variants were identified in 75/177 individuals (42.4%), biallelic MUTYH variants in 8 (4.5%), and alterations in BMPR1A and SMAD4 in two index cases each. Within the APC -positive subset, 52 unique germline variants were detected, including seven novel truncating frameshift mutations and six large genomic rearrangements. Segregation analysis supported pathogenicity in available families. Genotype–phenotype analyses showed a descriptive enrichment of truncating variants within the mutation cluster region (MCR) in classic FAP, whereas distal variants predominated in attenuated forms. This first large-scale Argentine study characterizes APC - and MUTYH -related polyposis in the region. The identification of novel APC alleles and regionally recurrent MUTYH variants broadens the national reference framework, providing critical evidence to improve genetic diagnosis and clinical management in this specific population.
