records.title: Tracking human HSCs and MPPs in mice reveals distinct clonal dynamics and responses to pre-transplant conditioning
records.abstract: Blood and immune cell regeneration is sustained by hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), which form the therapeutic basis of bone marrow transplantation. While the functional hierarchy of mouse HSPC subsets is well characterized, the distinct roles of human HSPC populations remain less well defined, particularly at clonal resolution and in the context of transplantation conditioning. Here, we performed quantitative clonal tracking of purified human HSCs (hHSCs) and human MPPs (hMPPs) in NSGW41 mice across primary and secondary transplantation under no conditioning, and busulfan or irradiation conditioning. We found that hHSC clones generated more blood cells, initiated lymphoid production earlier, and exhibited more robust multilineage differentiation than hMPP clones. hHSC clones were also less sensitive to conditioning, maintaining stable lineage biases. Notably, busulfan and irradiation differentially affected the magnitude, lineage bias, and timing of hematopoietic reconstitution without altering engraftment. During secondary transplantation, hHSCs and hMPPs contributed comparably to hematopoietic reconstitution but with substantially reduced output and increased clonal diversity. Extramedullary hematopoiesis was observed in all secondary recipients. records.title: Factors influencing exercise adherence among pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients: a cross-sectional study
records.abstract: Exercise adherence is crucial for rehabilitation in pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) recipients, yet remains challenging. This study investigated the current status and influencing factors of exercise adherence, focusing on symptom distress, exercise self-efficacy, and kinesiophobia. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 429 pediatric HSCT recipients. Sociodemographic Questionnaire, Exercise Adherence Scale (EAS), Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (ESES), the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale (MSAS10-18), and Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-11 (TSK-11) were administered. The mean EAS score was 35.77 ± 3.82. Multiple linear regression revealed that prior hospital-supervised exercise (β’ = 0.106, P = 0.003), pre-existing exercise habits (β’ = 0.147, P < 0.001), and daily screen time of 3–6 h (β’ = 0.081, P = 0.045) were protective factors. Daily screen time ≥ 6 h (β’ = -0.103, P = 0.023), fatigue (β’ = -0.169, P = 0.011), difficulty sleeping (β’ = -0.154, P = 0.001), nausea (β’ = -0.133, P = 0.013), and kinesiophobia (β’ = -0.171, P = 0.004) were negative predictors, while exercise self-efficacy (β’ = 0.156, P = 0.004) was a positive predictor. Pediatric HSCT recipients exhibit moderate exercise adherence. Individualized interventions targeting psychological and symptom-related barriers, along with structured screen time management, are needed.

records.abstract: Abstract Interactions between acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) cells and the bone marrow microenvironment can reduce responses to chemotherapy. Macrophages are abundant in AML bone marrow, but how macrophage-associated mitochondrial trafficking relates to drug tolerance remains incompletely defined. Using AML cell lines, primary AML specimens and monocyte-, iPSC- and mouse bone marrow-derived macrophage models, we found that M-CSF-differentiated macrophages attenuated daunorubicin-induced AML apoptosis, with the strongest protection during direct co-culture. Macrophage co-culture was also associated with increased AML respiratory capacity and reduced reactive oxygen species. Traditional diagnostic methods face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, and real-time applicability. Using a publicly sourced dataset of 500 class-labelled blood-smear images, the framework incorporates UNet++ with Attention Gates for segmentation, multi-resolution DeiT for feature extraction, and AE-MLP for AML, ALL, and healthy-cell classification. records.title: Cuproptosis as a candidate amplifier in ischemia/reperfusion injury: a metabolic-susceptibility framework and a graded appraisal of the evidence
records.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
records.abstract: Ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury involves multiple interconnected mechanisms, including mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and ferroptosis, whereas calcium overload and reactive oxygen species generation act as upstream injury signals rather than independent forms of regulated cell death. Cuproptosis is, at present, a weakly evidenced emerging candidate rather than a core mechanism on par with ferroptosis. Rather than centring cuproptosis, this review proposes a falsifiable metabolic-susceptibility framework and grades the existing evidence honestly. Its central premise is the dependence of cuproptosis on mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated metabolic proteins. During ischemia, suppression of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) activity and oxidative metabolism may reduce cuproptosis susceptibility without necessarily diminishing DLAT lipoylation. affiliations: Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University
records.abstract: Background Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are innate-like T lymphocytes that bridge innate and adaptive immunity. Objective To investigate the frequency, phenotype, function, and clinical relevance of MAIT cells, with a focus on CD8 + MAIT cells, in MM patients. Methods We analyzed peripheral blood (PB) and bone marrow (BM) samples from 120 MM patients (77 newly diagnosed, 22 in remission, 21 relapsed) and 30 healthy controls (HCs) using multi-color flow cytometry to assess MAIT cell frequency, subset distribution, activation (programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) expression), and effector function (cytokine production and cytotoxic molecule expression). Clinical parameters and survival outcomes were correlated with MAIT cell levels. Results MM patients demonstrated a significant reduction in total MAIT cell frequency, driven primarily by a loss of CD8 + MAIT cells. These cells exhibited a functional dysfunction phenotype marked by PD-1 upregulation. records.title: The MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis promotes alternative splicing-derived soluble PD-L1 generation and attenuates PD-L1 blockade efficacy in gastric cancer
records.abstract: Abstract Despite the clinical success of PD-1 blockade, the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in gastric cancer (GC) remains limited. Soluble PD-L1 (sPD-L1) has been proposed to function as a decoy that sequesters anti-PD-L1 antibodies, potentially contributing to therapeutic resistance. Our previous study identified an exon 5/6-skipping PD-L1 splice variant, designated PD-L1-v1, as an important source of sPD-L1 in GC. We also found that MAGOH is highly expressed in GC and participates in alternative splicing regulation. Here, we demonstrate that PD-L1-v1 acts as a soluble decoy that limits PD-L1 blocker binding to membrane-bound PD-L1 on tumor cells, thereby impairing the antitumor efficacy of PD-L1 blockade. Mechanistically, MAGOH upregulates hnRNPH1 expression, primarily by enhancing its mRNA stability, and promotes hnRNPH1-dependent exon5/6 skipping of PD-L1 pre-mRNA, thereby facilitating PD-L1-v1 and sPD-L1 generation. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism of resistance to PD-L1 blockade and highlight the MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis as a potential strategy for improving immunotherapy efficacy in GC.

records.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer
records.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outlines current computational and experimental techniques to identify, prioritise, and functionally validate non-coding variants in PDAC. We also emphasise new AI-based methods involving radiogenomics, AI imaging analysis and data integration, which provides novel potential to link genomic variation with phenotypic and imaging characteristics. records.title: [Emphasis on the standardization of initial treatment for ovarian cancer].
records.abstract: Based on the current technical development status among various regions and medical institutions in China, this article proposes corresponding clinical decision-making pathways to standardize and homogenize the initial treatment of ovarian cancer and optimize patient prognosis. All patients require comprehensive and thorough evaluation by the gynecologic oncology multidisciplinary team. Comprehensive staging surgery is indicated for early-stage ovarian cancer. For advanced cases, primary debulking surgery or interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is adopted based on clinical indications, with great emphasis on multidisciplinary expertise and surgical quality to elevate the implementation rate and complete resection rate of the initial debulking surgery. Standard first-line chemotherapy with adequate dosage and full cycles is strongly recommended. For advanced patients who have achieved remission after chemotherapy, genetic testing-guided maintenance therapy is preferred. Regular post-treatment follow-up is essential for early identification of tumor recurrence.

records.title: Alcohol use reduces the efficacy of anti-PD1 immunotherapy by disrupting antitumor immunity
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) has improved outcomes for some patients with advanced malignancies, but relatively few have a complete response. Alcohol use is common and impairs adaptive immunity. Here, we explored the link between alcohol use and ICI efficacy in mouse models of lung and bladder cancers and performed a retrospective assessment of a cohort of patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy. In both mouse models, a regimen of moderate-to-heavy ethanol intake reduced ICI efficacy by ∼50% and increased tumor recurrence. In patients with lung cancer, regular alcohol use was associated with reduced survival benefit from ICI. Effects were less definitive in patients with bladder cancer, melanoma, and head and neck cancer, in whom alcohol use reporting was too limited. In mice bearing MB49 bladder tumors, ethanol intake reduced the number of tumor-infiltrated T cells favoring T helper 17 cell (T H 17 cell) over T H 1 cell phenotypes in tumor-associated CD4 + T cells. It also reduced the number of tissue-resident memory T cells, increased the proportion of T cells expressing the alternative immune checkpoint receptor TIGIT, and induced SREBP-mediated lipid signaling in tumor-associated T cells. Blocking TIGIT with antibodies or, to a lesser extent, inhibiting SREBP signaling with betulin improved the efficacy of PD1 receptor blockade. records.title: GapCNV: A comprehensive framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data
affiliations: University of Florida Health Science Center
records.abstract: Copy number variants (CNVs) are prevalent in both diploid and haploid genomes and contribute to genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. However, CNV detection in low-input data, including low-cell and single-cell sequencing data, remains challenging due to the shallow and highly uneven read counts and amplification bias. Another challenge lies in selecting reference samples, which are used to provide a baseline for defining copy-number losses or gains. Normalization using references containing common CNVs can lead to cancellation of true CNV signals or false CNV calls. Here, we develop GapCNV, a statistical framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data from both haploid and diploid genomes. GapCNV uses preliminary cell clustering and shared CNV profiles to construct bin-specific pseudo-references from cells inferred to have the copy-neutral state. This strategy reduces the incorporation of common CNVs into the normalization baseline and thereby preserves common CNV signals. We evaluated GapCNV using simulations with and without amplification biases and datasets from Plasmodium falciparum , human breast cancer and melanoma. In simulations, GapCNV achieved high precision rate while maintaining competitive sensitivity, with advantages for detecting short and common CNVs. records.title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
records.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms. Echidna integrates genomic and transcriptomics data to reveal how copy number alterations shape tumor evolution and therapy resistance.

records.title: Rank-One Convexification for Quadratic Optimization Problems with Switching Constraints
records.abstract: We investigate convexification for convex quadratic optimization with switching constraints. Such problems can be cast as mixed-integer quadratic optimization problems, where binary variables are used to encode whether a linear inequality is active or not. First, we derive the convex hull for the epigraph of a quadratic function defined by a rank-one matrix and switching penalties. Using this rank-one convexification, we develop copositive and semidefinite relaxations for general convex quadratic functions. Leveraging these findings, we construct convex formulations to the support vector machine problem with 0–1 loss. The resulting methods scale well with the number of data points, provided that the number of features is small. In terms of statistical performance, the proposed methods outperform standard support vector machine problems with hinge loss in data sets corrupted by outliers. Funding: A. Gómez and S. Han was supported by the NUS (Suzhou) Research Institute [Grant SZ2025-03] and the Academic Research Fund Tier 1 from the Ministry of Education, Singapore [Grant FY2024]. records.title: Cell Communication Network factor 4 promotes tumor-induced immunosuppression in breast cancer
records.abstract: Cell Communication Network factor 4 (CCN4/WISP1) is a matricellular protein secreted by cancer cells that is upregulated in essentially all invasive breast cancers and promotes immunosuppression in melanoma. Limited anti-tumor immunity associates with poor patient outcomes in breast cancer, and elevated CCN4 correlates with dampened anti-tumor immunity in primary breast cancer tumors. To test for a direct causal link, we knocked out CCN4 in the Py230 and Py8119 syngeneic mouse breast cancer models. CCN4 knockout dramatically prolonged tumor-free survival in immunocompetent but not immunodeficient mice, establishing that CCN4's tumor-promoting effects are immune-dependent. In size-matched tumors, CCN4 knockout increases CD45+ infiltration and shifts the myeloid compartment from polymorphonuclear- to monocytic-myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), changes accompanied by a significant reduction in splenomegaly consistent with a systemic as well as local effect. CCN4 knockout produces convergent secretome changes across both breast cancer and melanoma cell lines, pointing to a conserved immunosuppressive program. Analysis of TCGA breast cancer data further reveals that genetic alterations converging on beta-catenin pathway activation, including CCN4 copy number amplification at a frequency comparable to ERBB2, are present in a substantial fraction of invasive breast cancers. records.title: Corilagin increases the sensitivity of neuroblastoma to cisplatin by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
records.abstract: Drug resistance remains the leading cause of cisplatin treatment failure in neuroblastoma (NB). This study aimed to investigate the potential of corilagin as an adjuvant therapy for overcoming cisplatin resistance in NB. In vitro functional assays—including cell viability (CCK-8), colony formation, transwell migration, and invasion assays—were conducted to evaluate the effects of corilagin in combination with cisplatin on human NB cell lines (SH-SY5Y and SK-N-BE(2)) and a cisplatin-resistant subline (SH-SY5Y/R). In vivo tumorigenesis experiments were performed to assess the suppressive effects of the corilagin-cisplatin combination on tumor growth initiated by SH-SY5Y and SH-SY5Y/R cells in mouse models. RNA sequencing was utilized to identify molecular mechanisms associated with cisplatin resistance and the therapeutic action of corilagin, followed by functional validation using 740Y-P, a specific agonist of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Our results showed that the combination of corilagin and cisplatin significantly inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and autophagic activity in SH-SY5Y/R cells, while robustly inducing apoptosis. Importantly, the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was found to be hyperactivated during the development of cisplatin resistance, whereas corilagin effectively suppressed this activation. These findings indicate that corilagin enhances cisplatin sensitivity in NB cells through modulation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

records.title: CosMxScope: scalable reconstruction and digital pathology integration of imaging-based CosMx spatial transcriptomics data

records.title: Laboratory Models of Hepatitis B and D Viruses: Search for Cell Permissiveness and Restriction Factors
records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is an oncogenic human pathogen that accounts for 250 mln cases of chronic hepatitis worldwide. Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) is its satellite that substantially aggravates liver disease. The development of new antivirals and the investigation of viral pathogenesis are limited by the absence of effective cellular and animal models. Current cell models are based on human primary hepatocytes, liver progenitor HepaRG cells, iPS-derived hepatocyte-like cells or various hepatoma cells overexpressing the putative NTCP receptor. However, in most of these models, a majority of cells are non-permissive. In this review, we briefly assess these models, summarize the approaches to the increasing infection rates, and discuss the data on proviral and antiviral (restriction) host factors. The data discussed suggest that rates of HBV and HDV infections are limited by hepatocyte polarization and insufficient expression of the NTCP receptor, as well as the existence of additional co-receptors and restriction factors that can act mostly on the virus entry stage.

However, the mechanisms driving cell clustering, and the role of phenotypic heterogeneity in the dynamics of these clusters, remain poorly understood. In this work, we propose a system of ordinary differential equations that models cluster formation dynamics within a coagulation–fragmentation–proliferation framework. Additionally, we provide preliminary insights into how clustering behaviour in co-cultures contrasts with that observed in monocultures. The model quantifies phenotypic differences in clustering dynamics: invasive cells in monoculture exhibit nearly threefold higher coagulation rates than proliferative cells, whereas proliferative cells display slightly higher proliferation rates. records.title: TIPE2 suppresses adipogenesis via METTL14-mediated m6A methylation and represents a potential therapeutic target for obesity
records.abstract: Abstract Despite conserved mechanisms maintaining energy homeostasis, the global obesity epidemic continues to rise. Tumor necrosis factor-α-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) is an anti-inflammatory regulator essential for immune homeostasis, yet its role in adipogenesis remains unclear. Here, we show that TIPE2 expression in human adipose tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index (BMI) and metabolic dysfunction. In mice, Tipe2 deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity, hyperglycaemia, and insulin resistance, whereas systemic AAV-mediated TIPE2 overexpression alleviates these phenotypes. In vitro, TIPE2 suppresses adipogenic differentiation in primary preadipocytes. Mechanistically, TIPE2 regulates N6-methyladenosine (m6A) via m6A methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14). Loss of TIPE2 reduces m6A levels and METTL14 expression, whereas METTL14 restoration reverses the pro-adipogenic effects. Furthermore, TIPE2 modulates adipogenesis through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) signaling. Together, these findings identify TIPE2 as a suppressor of adipogenesis via coordinated regulation of METTL14-dependent m6A modification and PPAR-γ signaling.

records.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
records.abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR–Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression. Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

records.title: 4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
records.abstract: Abstract Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Isolated phenotypes have been described for individual cell states, but how mitochondrial morphology and motility change across the full course of human tissue development has so far been unclear. Human stem cell-derived branching lung and intestinal organoids mimic developing human organs and make these systems accessible. Here we show, by imaging at key developmental time points from human stem cell through mature organoid tissue with lattice light-sheet microscopy, that mitochondrial networks adopt morphology and motility signatures that vary with developmental stage, that mitochondrial and cellular features can be used to predict developmental stage, and that two-dimensional measurements obscure features resolved only in three dimensions over time, yielding an integrated map of mitochondrial phenotypes across human tissue development.

records.title: InferPloidy enables CNV guided tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery from single cell RNA sequencing
records.abstract: Abstract Identifying malignant cells in single-cell gene expression data is essential for understanding tumor heterogeneity, but existing computational methods can be slow and perform inconsistently across datasets. Here, we present InferPloidy, a framework that combines graph-based cell grouping with iterative probabilistic modeling to distinguish cells with normal and altered chromosome copy numbers using profiles generated by InferCNV. Across breast, lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer datasets, the evaluated workflow reduces computation time by up to two orders of magnitude compared with existing tools and improves agreement with published cell annotations. This classification supports the identification of established therapeutic targets and candidate cell surface markers associated with tumor subtypes. The low proportion of unclassified cells helps preserve information for downstream analyses of gene expression differences and tumor population characteristics. These findings support InferPloidy as an efficient framework for tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery within the evaluated workflow. Its performance with inputs from other copy number inference methods requires further validation.

records.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics
records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location-level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell-state-associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co-organized hypoxic and extracellular-matrix-remodeling niche that co-localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene-centric descriptions of tissue structure.

records.title: Neuronal cell line expressing full-length mutant huntingtin displays alteration of proteasome activity
records.abstract: Polyglutamine diseases are incurable genetic neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of extended polyglutamine fragments-containing mutant proteins, which are prone to the formation of poorly soluble aggregates. The adequate cellular model is crucial in uncovering the pathological mechanisms responsible for neurotoxicity in Huntington’s disease (HD), screening for therapeutic molecules and elucidation of the molecular mechanisms impacted by particular compound. In the present study, genetic constructs based on the Sleeping Beauty system were created for the stable inducible expression of full-length normal and mutant huntingtin (HTT) in eukaryotic cells. These constructs were then employed to develop model neuronal cells using Neuro-2a cell line. The expression of HTT as well as the accumulation of HTT-immunopositive intracellular aggregates (most characteristic features of HD) was demonstrated, and these aggregates showed colocalization with the proteasome. The activation of the proteasome, as well as changes in the expression of proteasome regulators, components of the autophagy system, and the neuronal proteases cathepsins B and D, reflect the versatility of cellular responses to the mutant pathological forms of HTT.

affiliations: The First People's Hospital of Shunde
Shanghai Pudong New Area Gongli Hospital
records.abstract: Background The impact of clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), a novel cardiovascular risk factor, remains unclear in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), where cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the main cause of mortality. Methods We analysed data from 140,086 UK Biobank participants with MASLD. CHIP was identified via whole-exome sequencing. Incident CVD, including coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and heart failure (HF), was the primary outcome. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between CHIP and CVD risk. Results During a median 13.5-year follow-up, 15.7% of participants developed CVD. CHIP was associated with a higher risk of CVD (HR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09–1.23), with higher risks of stroke (HR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07–1.38) and HF (HR: 1.34, 95% CI: 1.21–1.49). Mutations in ASXL1, SRSF2, JAK2 , and SF3B1 were associated with a particularly high CVD risk. Additionally, a higher clonal haematopoiesis risk score (CHRS) was associated with incident CVD, CHD, stroke, and HF. In the three-category analysis, the P value for trend was significant for all outcomes, but the association was confined to large CHIP for CVD and CHD, whereas both CHIP categories showed elevated estimates for stroke and HF. Conclusions CHIP is independently associated with incident CVD in patients with MASLD. These findings support prospective evaluation of CHIP-informed cardiovascular risk stratification in this population.

records.journal: Journal of Lower Genital Tract Disease
records.abstract: Objectives: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among Kenyan women aged 15–44. records.title: Faith- and community-led service posts narrow HIV case finding, treatment and viral suppression gaps among men in Zambia, 2018–2022
affiliations: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
records.abstract: HIV testing and treatment coverage among men in Zambia remains suboptimal due to barriers that limit their engagement in care. We analyzed routine program data to assess HIV case finding, treatment initiation, retention, and viral load suppression among men attending Community Posts during two implementation periods: April 2018–March 2020 and April 2020–March 2022. Between 2018 and 2022, the number of Community Posts expanded from 9 to 38 nationwide. The proportion of men tested declined from 49.5% to 41.4%, while the proportion diagnosed (38.5% to 42.0%) and initiated on treatment (38.9% to 43.3%) increased significantly (p < 0.001). Community Posts improved HIV case finding, treatment initiation and viral suppression, even during the COVID-19 pandemic, supporting the potential of this scalable, faith- and community-led model to help close persistent HIV service gaps among men.

Tumor regions were manually segmented, and handcrafted radiomic features were extracted using a custom pipeline developed in Python. records.title: Targeted delivery of therapeutic retroviral replicating vectors to glioma using adipose-derived stem cells
records.abstract: Abstract Gene delivery using retroviral replicating vectors (RRVs) is highly efficient, with nearly full transduction occurring throughout tumors in small-animal glioma models. However, vector spread is still restricted by the dosage that can be delivered by a single injection of viral vector supernatant, particularly in the large and diffusely infiltrating tumors that are characteristic of human high-grade gliomas. This study attempted to further improve the efficacy of this approach by engineering adult human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) to function as the carrier and producer cells for RRVs. We investigated the capability of RRV-producing hASCs (hASC-RRVs) to yield RRVs and deliver the vector to gliomas. The results show that RRVs released from hASC-RRVs can efficiently infect glioma cells, achieving tumor-selective and persistent gene delivery to gliomas. We have also confirmed the tumor-tropic migratory ability of hASC-RRVs, which greatly improved the efficiency of RRV delivery in vivo . In addition, the therapeutic effect of RRVs delivered by hASCs was increased markedly. In an orthotopic mouse model of human glioma, after a single injection of hASC-RRVs, hASC-RRV-mediated prodrug activator gene therapy resulted in chronic suppression of tumor growth and prolonged survival of the animals. Thus, using hASCs as the carrier and producer for RRVs may represent a promising strategy for glioma gene therapy.

records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. records.abstract: Low muscle mass (LMM) is associated with poor outcomes in cancer, but its role in cancer development remains unclear. We examined pre-existing LMM and site-specific cancer incidence. We analyzed 4,441,403 adults who underwent national health screening in 2012. LMM was defined as the lowest sex-specific quartile of the predicted appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI). Cox models were used in men and women (<50 and ≥50 years), adjusting for demographic and clinical factors and body mass index (BMI). records.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of radiologists, with and without an artificial intelligence tool, at a tertiary cancer centre. Methods: The institutional review board considered this study at a tertiary cancer centre as a quality improvement project. Diagnostic performance metrics were assessed, including conditional sensitivity, conditional specificity and conditional area under the curve. records.title: Candidate gene prioritization through integration of public transcriptomic data and network analysis in sugarcane under water deficit
records.abstract: Climate change-induced water deficit significantly threatens sugarcane ( Saccharum spp.) yields, yet breeding for drought tolerance remains challenging due to its complex polyploid genome. Here, we demonstrate the value of reusing publicly available sugarcane transcriptomic data to explore gene expression profiles under drought. We propose a candidate gene prioritization framework, combining the integration of public transcriptome data and biological network mapping. Sixteen RNA-seq BioProjects of sugarcane grown under contrasting water conditions were retrieved from the SRA-NCBI repository. The 352 libraries were processed through a standardized analytical pipeline, and differential expression analyses were performed independently for each BioProject. The aggregated differentially expressed transcripts were subjected to functional enrichment analyses, revealing highly represented functional categories and candidate genes associated with stress-responsive pathways, notably involving abscisic acid signaling, raffinose biosynthesis, and key transcription factor families. The list of candidate genes was consolidated into 342 functionally coherent categories representing biologically related processes. records.title: The effects and toxicological responses of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate on the gill tissue of bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis)
records.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the acute and subchronic toxicity of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) on gill tissue of bighead carp ( Hypophthalmichthys nobilis ). The 96-h LC₅₀ was 9.43mg/L. Fish were exposed to 0, 0.47, 0.95, and 1.89 mg/L (0, 1/20, 1/10, 1/5 of LC₅₀) for 7, 14, and 21 days. SDBS caused dose- and time-dependent gill histopathology (lamellar fusion, epithelial lifting, mucous/chloride cell changes, inflammation). Biochemical assays showed increased MDA and reduced SOD, CAT, GPx activities, indicating severe oxidative stress. Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity was significantly suppressed. qPCR revealed downregulation of sod , ca t, gpx , nkaα1 , and upregulation of hsp70 , il-1β , tnf-α , and * bax/bcl-2 * ratio. Correlation analyses confirmed oxidative stress as the primary mechanism. These findings demonstrate that SDBS causes substantial gill damage via oxidative pathways, posing ecological risks to local freshwater ecosystems.

records.title: Uninformative non-reproduction: a pre-computable power frontier explains which driver–phenotype associations small cancer cohorts can and cannot test
records.abstract: Abstract Background Small cancer cohorts are routinely used to test driver–phenotype associations, and negative results from them enter the literature as evidence that no association exists. Reproducibility frameworks classify such results only as reproduced or not reproduced, conflating a genuine null finding with a study that could never have detected the effect. We asked whether this third possibility can be identified before data are collected. Methods We derived a closed-form detection frontier, d min (n,p) — the smallest standardised effect detectable at 80% power, two-sided α = 0.05, in a two-group comparison of total size n with alteration prevalence p — and calibrated it against empirical power by simulation across three data-generating mechanisms and four group-size configurations (60 points, 2 000 replicates each). We then applied the frontier to a complete scan of nine driver variables against eight expression signatures in TCGA malignant pleural mesothelioma ( n = 87), and to fifteen rare-tumour TCGA cohorts. Results Under ideal-normal data the closed form was accurate to 0.009; under skew and dropout contamination it over-estimated the detection limit by up to 0.086, erring on the safe side in all eight non-normal configurations. records.abstract: SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2 E76K and Mek1 DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2 C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2 C459S , SHP2 E76K , and SHP2 C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2 C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K markedly rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus in mutant mice. records.abstract: Background First-line R-CHOP immunochemotherapy controls diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in most patients, but 30%–40% develop primary refractory disease or early relapse, both with poor survival. Methods We conducted a comprehensive literature search in ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed through August 28, 2026, using predefined Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms and keywords related to CAR-T, TRUCKs, toxicity, and cancer. Although treatment-induced senescence (TIS) effectively suppresses cancer cell proliferation, the long-term accumulation of the immunosuppressive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) promotes immune evasion, leading to the failure of immunotherapy. Herein, a liposomal nanoparticle (T-Lipo@Das/Ber) encapsulating the ATR inhibitor Berzosertib and the Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitor Dasatinib was designed, which can target prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). T-Lipo@Das/Ber efficiently enters cells via PSMA-mediated endocytosis. On the one hand, Berzosertib inhibits ATR, increases DNA damage, and induces the release of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory factors via the cGAS-STING pathway, ultimately enhancing tumor immunogenicity. On the other hand, by inhibiting the Src/Bcr-Abl pathway, Dasatinib reprograms the SASP, reducing the secretion of immunosuppressive factors while promoting the exposure of calreticulin (CRT) and the release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), thereby synergistically recruiting and activating immune cells. records.title: Steroid Hormone Receptor Isoform Diversity in Gynecologic Oncogenesis: Mechanisms, Biomarker Evidence, and Implications for Precision Oncology.
affiliations: Division of Cancer Research and Therapeutics, Yenepoya Research Centre, Yenepoya (Deemed to be University), Mangalore 575018, India.
records.abstract: Aberrant regulation of steroid hormone receptors (SHRs) can alter transcriptional programs relevant to gynecologic tumor initiation, progression, and treatment response. Importantly, receptor diversity arises through biologically distinct mechanisms, including alternative pre-mRNA splicing, alternative promoter usage, alternative translation initiation, and post-translational modification; receptor subtypes encoded by different genes should not be considered splice variants. This narrative review focuses on estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), androgen receptor (AR), glucocorticoid receptor (GR), and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) diversity in ovarian, endometrial, cervical, vulvar, and related gynecologic malignancies. Evidence is organized by tumor type and interpreted according to its level of support, distinguishing mechanistic preclinical observations from patient associations, candidate biomarkers, and clinically evaluated therapeutic strategies. Breast-cancer studies are used only as comparative mechanistic context when directly relevant to SHR isoform biology. Current evidence is strongest for ER- and PR-related receptor forms, whereas gynecologic data for AR, GR, and especially MR variants remain limited. Clarifying the molecular origin, tumor-specific function, and clinical validation of individual receptor forms will be essential before isoform-directed approaches can be incorporated into precision gynecologic oncology.

records.title: Truncating variants reveal functional divergence of the SAMD9 and SAMD9L paralogues.
affiliations: Department of Medicine Huddinge, Center for Hematology and Regenerative Medicine, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden.
records.abstract: Germline gain-of-function (GoF) variants in the paralogous sterile alpha motif domain containing 9 (SAMD9) and SAMD9-like (SAMD9L) genes cause myelodysplasia, primary immunodeficiencies, and neurological disorders. Predicting the functional consequences of individual variants, however, remains challenging, owing partly to the complexity of these large, multidomain proteins. Here, we functionally characterized several rare patient-derived SAMD9/9L variants, identifying multiple novel GoF and loss-of-function (LoF) variants, including SAMD9L p.C883X-the shortest documented SAMD9L GoF truncation within the NTPase domain. SAMD9L NTPase domain truncations are associated with severe, early-onset pathology, yet despite the high structural and sequence similarity between the two proteins, analogous truncating variants have not been reported in SAMD9 patients. To examine whether this reflects a fundamental difference, we generated multiple homologous SAMD9 truncations, which, unlike their SAMD9L counterparts, exhibited LoF rather than GoF activity. Additionally, established computational pathogenicity predictors failed to identify pathogenic variants or distinguish GoF from LoF. Collectively, these results demonstrate that functional outcomes in SAMD9/9L cannot be reliably inferred from sequence, structure, or computational prediction alone, underscoring the importance of empirical characterization.

affiliations: Division of Surgery, Gastrointestinal Center Yokohama Shin-Midori General Hospital Kanagawa Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are used as a bridge to surgery (BTS) or for palliation (PAL) in malignant colorectal obstruction, but high axial force may contribute to perforation. We prospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of the low-axial-force Naturfit colonic stent in both settings. Methods This prospective multicenter single-arm study enrolled 208 patients at 11 Japanese institutions between 2019 and 2022 (BTS, n = 137; PAL, n = 71). The primary endpoint was clinical success of colorectal stenting; secondary endpoints included technical success, adverse events, surgical outcomes after BTS stenting, and 12-month palliative outcomes. Results Technical success and clinical success of colorectal stenting were both 99.0%, with perforation in three patients (1.4%). In the BTS cohort, clinical success of BTS was 97.1%; no perforations occurred, and early and late adverse-event rates were 1.5% and 3.7%. All patients underwent elective surgery; colostomy and laparoscopic surgery rates were 4.4% and 87.6%. In the palliative cohort, clinical success of colorectal stenting was 98.6%, late adverse events occurred in 16.9%, and 12-month overall survival and stent patency were 46.6% and 67.6%. Conclusions Naturfit achieved high technical and clinical success of colorectal stenting with a low perforation rate. records.title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
affiliations: Key Laboratory of Polymer Chemistry and Physics of Ministry of Education, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Peking University, Beijing, 100871, China.
records.abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8 + T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

records.title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Oita Red Cross Hospital Oita Japan.
records.abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

records.abstract: Rural patients in the United States face disproportionate gynecologic cancer mortality compared to urban patients, driven by overlapping geographic, socioeconomic, and structural barriers that vary across cancer types and the care continuum. This review synthesizes the literature on rural disparities in cervical, endometrial, and ovarian cancers from prevention through survivorship. Rurality is defined variably across the literature, most commonly using government classification systems such as Rural-Urban Continuum Codes or Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Rural women experience lower Human Papillomavirus vaccination rates and reduced uptake of guideline-concordant cervical cancer screening, higher rates of late-stage ovarian cancer diagnosis, and delayed endometrial cancer diagnosis. Even when rural patients access subspecialist care, treatment quality gaps persist, including higher rates of open surgical staging for endometrial cancer and reduced access to brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer. Survival disparities remain even among rural patients treated at tertiary centers with subspecialist involvement, underscoring that geographic access alone is insufficient. Insurance status, health literacy, financial hardship, and limited social support compound these barriers throughout the continuum. records.abstract: This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints. Young's modulus should therefore not be regarded as an isolated universal cancer biomarker, but rather as one component of a dynamic mechanophenotype influenced by disease stage, cellular region, microenvironment and measurement methodology. records.title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
affiliations: Key Laboratory of Microbial Pathogenesis and Interventions of Fujian Province University, Biomedical Research Center of South China, College of Life Sciences, Fujian Normal University, 1 Keji Road, Fuzhou, 350117, China.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo , FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

records.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a WHO grade IV brain tumor with aggressive growth and frequent recurrence, and temozolomide (TMZ) remains the standard first-line chemotherapy despite limited durable benefits. Parthenolide (Pt), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from the medicinal plant feverfew, has shown antitumor activity in multiple cancer types; however, its therapeutic potential and downstream mechanisms in GBM have not been fully defined. Herein, we demonstrate that Pt induces apoptosis, suppresses stemness, and reduces invasion in human U-87MG and T98G cells. Pt also potentiates TMZ's efficacy in vitro and in an orthotopic GBM model with male NOD-SCID mice. RNA-sequencing and pathway analyses revealed that Pt markedly represses epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated programs. Among the most significantly downregulated genes, transgelin-2 (TAGLN2) emerged as a key Pt-responsive target, and its high expression was correlated with poor survival in glioma cohorts. Mechanistically, inhibitor screening identified glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β) as a critical upstream regulator of Pt-induced TAGLN2 repression. records.title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
affiliations: Department of Clinical Laboratory, Ganzhou People's Hospital, Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, 341000, China. Electronic address: yuluhu@163.com.
records.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

records.abstract: Outpatient gynecologic procedures are core competencies for generalist clinicians and support access to comprehensive preventive and reproductive care. This review summarizes key outpatient gynecologic procedures, including cervical cancer screening, insertion and removal of intrauterine devices and contraceptive implants, and endometrial biopsies. Evidence-based approaches to pain management for intrauterine procedures are reviewed, including intracervical and paracervical blocks. Procedural pitfalls and strategies to reduce complications are discussed. Competence in these procedures enables timely, patient-centered preventative and reproductive care while minimizing need for specialist referral.

records.abstract: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT has become an essential complementary modality in the management of gynecologic malignancies, combining metabolic and anatomic information beyond the morphologic limitations of CT and MRI. This review examines its clinical roles and diagnostic limitations across cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar, and vaginal cancers, focusing on nodal staging, recurrence detection, treatment response assessment, and prognostication. Its distinct strengths-nodal staging in cervical cancer and recurrence detection in endometrial and ovarian cancers-are highlighted alongside key interpretive pitfalls. Emerging approaches, including PET/MRI, volumetric parameters, FAPI and other novel radiopharmaceuticals, and radiomics, are discussed as future directions in gynecologic oncology.

records.title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
affiliations: New Technologies Research Centre, University of West Bohemia in Pilsen, 30100, Pilsen, Czech Republic.
records.abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

records.title: Inhaled nanogels ameliorate vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension <i>via</i> normalization of endothelia-smooth muscle cell crosstalk.
affiliations: Basic Medical Research Center, The Third Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Changzhou, 213003, China.
records.abstract: Maintaining appropriate vascular nitric oxide (NO) levels in pulmonary arteries is crucial for the alleviation of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, in the injured vascular microenvironment, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) deplete NO to generate peroxynitrite, which aggravates the oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Herein, ROS-responsive, zwitterionic nanogels (NGs), containing arginine pendants as NO precursors and encapsulating resveratrol (RSV) as an anti-oxidant, were developed for PAH management via inhalation. Benefiting from their zwitterionic surface that repels mucin adsorption, the inhaled NGs exhibit effective pulmonary mucus penetration and mucosal absorption, enabling robust diffusion to the injured pulmonary arteries. In the oxidative vascular microenvironment, the diselenide crosslinkers within the NGs are cleaved, promoting NGs dissociation and on-demand RSV release. The released RSV scavenges ROS and the arginine pendants are oxidized to generate NO, which cooperate to interrupt the ROS/NO disequilibrium. A 78-year-old woman underwent anterior sectionectomy for recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma and developed persistent bile leakage. The infected biloma showed significant shrinkage, and the patient was discharged without complications. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. This review therefore starts from clinical biological and mechanical failure phenotypes and asks a different question: when is bioactivation mechanically safe? We define mechanically safe bioactivation as a functional improvement in bone or soft tissue response that does not meaningfully reduce defect tolerance, phase stability, fatigue resistance, interfacial durability, or full implant integrity. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to September 25, 2026, was used to construct an evidence map and identify finite processing windows for surface treatments and for material and structural reinforcement, rather than treating greater roughness, porosity, stabilization, or multifunctionality as inherently beneficial. Across the available evidence, the most defensible direction is to localize biological functions within mechanically supported regions while protecting the load-bearing core and critical tensile stress sites. records.abstract: Engineering artificial dendritic cells (DCs) holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy, but achieving spatiotemporally controlled multifunctionality within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remains a challenge. Here, we report a chemically engineered, ultrasound (US)-activatable artificial DCs nanosystem (nDC-M) that mimics the DC-mediated T-cell immunity through a rationally designed molecular assembly. The nDC-M integrates three key functional modules including a semiconducting polymer nanoparticle and interleukin-2 (IL-2) crosslinked by hypoxia-cleavable fragment for on-demand cytokine release upon US trigger, a matured DC membrane cloak for tumor cell recognition and a surface-anchored maleimide (MAL) group for covalent antigen capture and presentation. Under US treatment, sonodynamic effect of semiconducting polymer ablates tumors and consumes oxygen to allow breakage of hypoxia-cleavable fragments, leading to IL-2 leakage. This nDC-M exhibits a comprehensive and conferred mimicking functions including tumor cell recognition, antigen presentation and sono-activatable cytokine secretion. In bilateral breast cancer and lung metastasis models, US-driven nDC-M therapy significantly suppresses tumor progression and metastasis. Moreover, combining nDC-M with checkpoint blockade achieves complete eradication of local and distant tumors and establishes long-term immunological memory against recurrence. records.abstract: Background Reliable and reproducible orthotopic GL261 glioma models are essential for preclinical glioblastoma research, particularly for evaluating therapeutic strategies in immunocompetent mice. However, conventional intracranial implantation of GL261 cells frequently results in variable tumor engraftment and heterogeneous tumor growth, limiting experimental reproducibility and increasing variability in therapeutic studies. New method We developed an optimized Matrigel-assisted orthotopic GL261 glioma model by incorporating Matrigel into the conventional intracranial implantation procedure. Tumor establishment and progression were evaluated using bioluminescence imaging and micro-computed tomography, followed by histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses. records.title: Target-responsive "signal-down" electrochemical biosensor based on an anti-biofouling hydrogel for glutathione detection.
affiliations: Shanghai Key Laboratory of Functional Materials Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China University of Science and Technology, Shanghai, 200237, People's Republic of China.
records.abstract: Glutathione (GSH), a ubiquitous biothiol, is critical in physiological processes, and abnormal fluctuations in its level are intimately associated with various diseases. However, real-time in vivo monitoring of GSH within tissues, such as the tumor microenvironment (TME), is fundamentally hindered by severely electrode biofouling and electrochemical interference from structural analogs. Herein, we report a novel target-responsive "Signal-Down" electrochemical biosensor based on an anti-biofouling hydrogel for GSH detection, which elegantly integrates robust anti-biofouling capabilities with highly specific target recognition. This sensing interface features a highly hydrated polyacrylamide (PAM) network, crosslinked by disulfide bonds and loaded with ferrocene/β-cyclodextrin (Fc@β-CD) electroactive probes. Upon exposure to GSH, the highly specific thiol-disulfide exchange reaction triggers the macroscopic degradation of the Fc-hydrogel. This spatial disruption drives the rapid outward diffusion of the redox probes, translating microscopic molecular recognition into a dramatic attenuation of the electrochemical signal. records.title: USF1 promotes growth and glycolysis in acute myeloid leukemia cells.
affiliations: Department of Immunology, Basic Medical School, Guizhou Medical University, Guiyang, Guizhou, 561113, China.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematological malignancy characterized by impaired hematopoiesis and aggressive progression, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis, especially in elderly patients. Metabolic reprogramming, particularly enhanced glycolysis, is a hallmark of AML and contributes to disease progression and therapy resistance. Upstream stimulatory factor 1 (USF1) regulates metabolism, the cell cycle, and oncogenesis in solid tumors, whereas its role in AML remains unclear. Herein, we investigated the role and underlying mechanism of USF1 in regulating USP25 transcription and promoting AML progression. We found that USF1 was highly expressed in AML samples and cell lines, and its elevated expression was associated with poor prognosis. Functional assays showed that USF1 promoted AML cell growth and glycolysis while inhibiting apoptosis. Mechanistically, USF1 directly bound to the USP25 promoter, enhancing its transcription. Knockdown of USP25 reversed the tumor-promoting effects of USF1. Moreover, in vivo studies demonstrated that silencing USF1 significantly inhibited tumor growth. In conclusion, USF1 promotes AML cell growth and glycolysis through the transcriptional activation of USP25, thereby identifying the USF1-USP25 axis as a potential therapeutic target for AML.

records.title: Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series.
affiliations: Wolfson Unit for Endoscopy, St Mark's The National Bowel Hospital London UK.
records.abstract: Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy-synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro-bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. Complete procedural videos were reviewed to describe treated visible submucosal vessel burden, minor bleeding, episodes of transient loss of visualization, and hemostatic forceps use. En bloc and histologically margin-negative (R0) resection was achieved in all 10 cases, while curative endoscopic resection was achieved in nine cases (90%). No intraprocedural perforation, delayed bleeding, post-ESD coagulation syndrome, or unplanned repeat intervention occurred. Median lesion size was 55 mm (interquartile range, 40-69.5), median procedure duration was 102.5 min (100-167.5), and median treated visible vessel count was 21 (11.5-40.75), corresponding to 1.04 vessels/cm 2 (0.64-1.74). Minor bleeding and transient loss of visualization occurred during procedures but were controlled endoscopically. Hemostatic forceps were required therapeutically for active bleeding from one vessel across the series, and no procedure required abandonment or conversion to surgery. Electronic address: Claudia.kirsch@yale.edu.
records.abstract: In head and neck imaging somatostatin receptor (SSTR) imaging with DOTATATE has markedly improved detection of meningiomas compared to schwannomas as well as preoperative surgical or radiation therapy planning and posttreatment surveillance. DOTATATE is great for detection of paragangliomas, pituitary tumors, olfactory neuroblastoma, neuroendocrine neoplasms and medullary thyroid cancer. DOTATATE is useful in identifying multiple paragangliomas especially if hereditary, multiple endocrine tumors in genetic syndromes and medullary thyroid cancer and may potentially assessment of middle ear adenomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors and olfactory neuroblastoma. SSTR PET may help predict response to targeted tumor treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

records.title: Clinical Outcomes of Double Half-Pigtail Versus Straight Plastic Stents for Endoscopic Biliary Drainage of Malignant Distal Biliary Obstruction.
affiliations: Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatology Saga Medical Center Koseikan Saga Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives The clinical performance of double half-pigtail plastic stents (DHPs) for malignant distal biliary obstruction (MDBO) remains unclear. We compared DHPs with straight plastic stents (STs) regarding the timing, incidence, and causes of recurrent biliary obstruction (RBO). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography-guided transpapillary single plastic stent placements for MDBO performed between October 2022 and March 2026. For the primary analysis, only initial stenting episodes were included. The primary endpoint was the time to RBO (TRBO), which was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and log-rank methods. Results A total of 131 stent-placement episodes in 86 patients were eligible. The primary analysis included 72 patients undergoing initial stenting, comprising 20 patients in the DHP group and 52 patients in the ST group. The DHP and ST groups had a similar median TRBO (116 vs. 119 days; log-rank p = 0.726), incidence of RBO (40.0% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.638), and incidence of stent occlusion (40.0% vs. 32.7%; p = 0.560). No migration occurred with DHPs, whereas seven migration events occurred with STs (0% vs. 13.5%; p = 0.084). Both groups had similar adverse event rates (0% vs. 11.5%; p = 0.113). Conclusions DHPs did not prolong the TRBO or reduce its incidence compared with STs. However, migration-related RBO occurred only with STs. The potential advantage of DHPs may be a lower incidence of stent migration

records.abstract: Cervical cancer, the fourth most frequent malignancy in women worldwide, continues to be a major public health concern. Around 90% of high-grade cervical cancer cases are linked to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV). This phenotype, histologically, includes two major subtypes of cervical cancer: squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. Drug resistance poses a major hurdle to treatment because it targets the apoptotic pathway. To overcome this, there is an urgent need for alternative routes to a curative strategy. Here, we focused on identifying non-apoptotic cell death pathways as a potential therapeutic option. Bulk RNA sequencing data for cervical cancer samples were obtained from the TCGA-CESC dataset. We combined gene set enrichment analysis, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning, which revealed ferroptosis as a key vulnerability at the bulk RNA level. Single-cell RNA sequencing data further confirmed the expression of ferroptosis-related components, including SCC and ADC. Subsequent analyses focused on identifying key regulators of the ferroptosis pathway. Further dissection of ferroptosis regulators and PSAT1 was prioritized as a prime translational target in adenocarcinoma compared with squamous cell carcinoma. To advance therapeutic translation, we applied AI-driven de novo compound generation to design a candidate drug targeting PSAT1.
